messages:
maya: Heads up - customer redwood-analytics reported SSE stream truncation on /v1/streams (text-generation). request_id=cr-10e4b2. They see the stream abruptly stop and the client ends up with a partial JSON: no final finish_reason and no 'data: [DONE]'. Frequency ~0.12% but reproducible for a specific long prompt. Repro steps below.

support_ash: Can you paste request id + minimal repro and any edge logs?

maya: Request id: cr-10e4b2. Minimal repro (curl):

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"<long prompt here>","stream":true}'
```

Client output (truncated):
```
data: {"id":"c1","object":"token","text":"...","finish_reason":
```
and then connection closes. The JSON is cut mid-value. No 'data: [DONE]'.

dev-bot: Deploy log: no runtime code changes at 2026-03-07T03:14:22Z.

ops_jordan: Could be ingress LB sending RST/FIN or runtime not flushing. Can you capture tcpdump of the client connection and paste the last few bytes + edge logs around cr-10e4b2? Also check for SIGPIPE/OOM on the runtime.

maya: Pasted trimmed tcpdump hex (client side):
```
... 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 22 63 31 22 2c 22 6f 62 6a 22 3a 22 74 6f 6b 65 6e 22 2c 22 74 65 78 74 22 3a 22 2e 2e 2e 2c 22 66 69 6e 69 73 68 5f 72 65 61 73 6f 6e 22 3a
```
Which decodes to: '{"id":"c1","obj":"token","text":"...,"finish_reason":' and then EOF.

samir: Thanks. That pattern points to the runtime performing a write that's partially delivered when the TCP connection is closed by the peer (likely the LB). Two suspects: (1) ingress proxy/ALB closing idle streaming connections aggressively; (2) runtime crash/oom before final flush.

ops_jordan: Edge logs show a FIN from the LB at the same ms as the truncated write for that request. LB pool for streaming had idle_timeout=15s in one zone; we should increase for streaming lanes. Also searching for OOM/SIGABRT on the runtime shows none around that PID.

support_ash: Short-term mitigation for customers: implement client-side resume using Last-Event-ID + idempotent session tokens, or do automatic reconnects that request missing tokens. Also increase LB idle_timeout for customer-specific routes.

maya: Customer tried naive reconnect without Last-Event-ID and saw duplicated tokens (client had to dedupe). They want server-side resume semantics.

samir: Action items summarized: 
- eng-runtime: ensure SSE buffer flush on connection close and explicitly write a final newline and 'data: [DONE]' if possible to avoid mid-JSON cutoffs. (samir)
- eng-infra: bump LB idle_timeout for streaming pools to 120s and enable TCP keepalive; add a routing rule to prefer longer-lived connections for known streaming customers. (ops_jordan)
- support: provide the customer with a robust resume example (Last-Event-ID + session token guidance). (support_ash)
I've opened INC-2026-03-SSE12 and PR #3421 (runtime: flush sse buffer on close).

dev-bot: PR #3421 created by @samir: 'runtime: flush sse buffer on close + tests'

maya: Customer accepted the workaround and will enable client-side resume. They asked for ETA on server patch and confirmation that we won't deliver malformed final JSON.

support_ash: Marking escalated to eng. Assigning to samir.

samir: Will roll the flush patch to canary tonight and monitor metric 'dropped_final_chunk' for reduction. If canary is stable, promote to prod and revert LB change if unnecessary.

ops_jordan: Added a note: for this customer we enabled header 'x-sse-trace: true' to log stream-level events and will keep trace for 72h.

maya: Great, thanks everyone :thumbsup: Keeping thread open for 48h and will post follow-ups.
